title.en: Streamline flow and the equation of continuity

heading.en: Why do you squeeze the end of a garden hose?

hook.en: Press your thumb over the end of a hose and the water shoots much farther. The same water must squeeze through a smaller opening, so it goes faster.
hook.kn: ಪೈಪಿನ ತುದಿಯನ್ನು ಹೆಬ್ಬೆರಳಿನಿಂದ ಒತ್ತಿದರೆ ನೀರು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ದೂರ ಚಿಮ್ಮುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದೇ ನೀರು ಚಿಕ್ಕ ತೆರೆಯುವಿಕೆಯಿಂದ ಹೊರಬರಬೇಕಾದ್ದರಿಂದ ವೇಗ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Flow is steady when the velocity of the fluid at each point does not change with time. The path a fluid particle follows is a streamline. In steady flow streamlines never cross, because a particle at a point can have only one velocity. Above a critical speed the flow becomes turbulent, with eddies.
body.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಬಿಂದುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ ವೇಗ ಕಾಲದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗದಿದ್ದರೆ ಹರಿವು ಸ್ಥಿರ. ದ್ರವ ಕಣದ ಪಥವೇ ಧಾರಾರೇಖೆ. ಧಾರಾರೇಖೆಗಳು ಎಂದಿಗೂ ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಕ್ರಾಂತಿಕ ವೇಗ ಮೀರಿದರೆ ಹರಿವು ಪ್ರಕ್ಷುಬ್ಧವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Why narrow pipes give fast jets

say.en: Water flows steadily through a pipe that narrows. In steady flow, streamlines never cross.
At the wide end, area A₁ and slow speed v₁. At the narrow end, area A₂ and fast speed v₂.
In time Δt, the volume A₁v₁Δt enters and A₂v₂Δt leaves. A liquid cannot pile up, so these are equal.

draw.tex: A_1 v_1 \Delta t = A_2 v_2 \Delta t

say.en: This is the equation of continuity: A v is constant. The volume flow rate is the same at every section.
A hose of diameter 2 centimetre carries water at 1 metre per second. Squeeze the nozzle to half a centimetre: the speed becomes 16 metres per second.
Speed falls as one over d squared: halve the diameter and the speed is four times as large.

narration.en: Water flows steadily through a pipe that narrows. In steady flow, streamlines never cross. At the wide end, area A₁ and slow speed v₁. At the narrow end, area A₂ and fast speed v₂. In time Δt, the volume A₁v₁Δt enters and A₂v₂Δt leaves. A liquid cannot pile up, so these are equal. This is the equation of continuity: A v is constant. The volume flow rate is the same at every section. A hose of diameter 2 centimetre carries water at 1 metre per second. Squeeze the nozzle to half a centimetre: the speed becomes 16 metres per second. Speed falls as one over d squared: halve the diameter and the speed is four times as large.

An incompressible liquid cannot pile up, so the same volume passes every cross-section each second: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂. Where the pipe is narrow the liquid moves faster. The dots are bits of liquid moving with the flow.
narration.kn: ಸಂಕುಚಿಸಲಾಗದ ದ್ರವ ಎಲ್ಲೂ ಶೇಖರವಾಗದು, ಹಾಗಾಗಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ಸೆಕೆಂಡ್ ಪ್ರತಿ ಅಡ್ಡಕೊಯ್ತದ ಮೂಲಕ ಅದೇ ಗಾತ್ರ ಹಾದುಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂. ಕೊಳವೆ ಕಿರಿದಾದಲ್ಲಿ ದ್ರವ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಚುಕ್ಕೆಗಳು ಹರಿವಿನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಚಲಿಸುವ ದ್ರವದ ತುಣುಕುಗಳು.

body.en: For an incompressible fluid in steady flow, the volume entering one end of a tube each second equals the volume leaving the other: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂. Where the pipe is narrow the fluid moves fast; where it is wide it moves slowly. This is conservation of mass.
body.kn: ಅಸಂಪೀಡ್ಯ ದ್ರವಕ್ಕೆ A₁v₁ = A₂v₂. ಪೈಪ್ ಕಿರಿದಾದಲ್ಲಿ ವೇಗ ಹೆಚ್ಚು, ಅಗಲವಾದಲ್ಲಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ. ಇದು ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಯ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ.

heading.en: Halve the radius, four times the speed

body.en: Because v ∝ 1/r², halving the radius of a pipe makes the speed four times; a third of the radius makes it nine times.
